thread:
amanda.s: Hey team — customer (AcmeGames) keeps seeing intermittent 429s when sending long replay contexts (~40k tokens). Happening only on rwd3-large, not on rwd3-medium. They say it spikes during user replay import.
amanda.s: Sample error: `429 rate_limit_exceeded`. Attached request-id: rq_0a1b2c3d4e.
amanda.s: They sent a few dozen requests in a short window, but our docs say RPM/TPS should handle bursts. Can someone triage? :melting_face:

devin.k: Thanks — can you paste the raw response headers and a simple curl repro? Also which API endpoint are they hitting (chat/generate/embeddings)?
amanda.s: Chat generate, POST /v1/chat/completions. Minimal repro they shared:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd3-large","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"..."}],"max_tokens":1024,"context":"<~40k tokens>"}'
```

amanda.s: Response body (redacted):
```json
{"error":{"type":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"Per-model rate limit exceeded"},"request_id":"rq_0a1b2c3d4e"}
```
Headers from the response (customer saved):
```
x-rwd-rpm-limit: 1200
x-rwd-rpm-remaining: 0
x-rwd-tpm-limit: 60000
x-rwd-tpm-remaining: 52000
x-rwd-concurrency-limit: 6
x-rwd-concurrency-remaining: 0
x-rwd-context-max-tokens: 65536
x-rwd-context-current-tokens: 40212
x-rwd-queue-pos: 0
```

ops-jon: Looks like RPM window exhausted (remaining 0) — they hit the RPM cap even though TPM is fine. Also concurrency remained 0 meaning they probably had >=6 simultaneous streams at that instant. The large context increases per-request token accounting so fewer requests burn the RPM faster.

mike.b: Two quick checks: 1) Are they doing many parallel workers? Concurrency limit is per-model per-customer. 2) Is this short burst pattern (lots of small intervals) or sustained? If short burst, our burst window still counts toward RPM.

amanda.s: They said an import job fanouts 12 workers that each send ~8 requests over 10s to precompute replays. So yes parallel and bursty.

devin.k: Repro steps I ran locally with a scripted fanout (6 parallel curl loops) and hit 429s within ~20s against rwd3-large. Log excerpt: 
```
[2026-02-05T14:12:20Z] POST /v1/chat  status=200  req=rq_xxx  tokens=39000
[2026-02-05T14:12:22Z] POST /v1/chat  status=200  req=rq_xxy  tokens=40200
[2026-02-05T14:12:24Z] POST /v1/chat  status=429  req=rq_0a1b2c3d4e  error=rate_limit_exceeded
[2026-02-05T14:12:25Z] POST /v1/chat  status=429  req=rq_zzzz  error=rate_limit_exceeded
```

ops-jon: That matches RPM exhaustion. Note: our RPM counts each request equally, not normalized by context size, but large contexts consume TPM and also cause higher memory use which triggers lower concurrency headroom. So two levers: RPM and concurrency.

devin.k: For customers hitting this regularly, recommended mitigations:
- Reduce parallelism (limit workers to <= concurrency_limit)
- Add exponential backoff on 429s (Retry-After header may not always be present for per-model RPM)
- Batch messages where possible (combine several small requests into one up-front request)
- Reduce context length or trim chat history before sending
- Use model variant with higher concurrency/RPM profile (e.g., rwd3-medium tolerates more parallelism) or request Dedicated capacity

mike.b: Also ask support to check for auth/tenant mixups — RPM and concurrency are scoped by API key/tenant. If they rotate keys across workers they can accidentally multiply quotas.

amanda.s: I asked them — they confirmed a single API key shared across 12 runners.

devin.k: Ok that explains it. 12 workers * bursts * each request counts toward RPM -> they hit the 1200 RPM cap quickly. For example: 12 workers * 8 requests in 10s => 576 requests in that 10s window which scales to >3000 RPM rate when extrapolated from bursts.

amanda.s: They asked whether context length effects throttling aside from TPM. They see 429s when context hits ~40k even though tpm_remaining still looked high.

ops-jon: Context impacts internal scheduling: large contexts increase inference time and RPC duration, which raises concurrent slots used longer. That pushes concurrency_remaining to 0 sooner. The per-model concurrency limit is typically lower for large memory models, so even with RPM headroom you can still see 429s if concurrency is saturated. The headers you pasted show concurrency_remaining=0.

devin.k: Diagnostic checklist to send to customer: 
1) Capture one full failing request/response pair with headers and request_id.
2) Share a short timeline: how many workers, how many requests each, frequency.
3) Try throttling concurrency client-side to 4 and see if errors stop.
4) Try trimming context to under 20k tokens and compare.

amanda.s: I sent the checklist. They tried reducing parallelism to 4 and errors disappeared. They also tested trimming context to ~18k and throughput improved.

billing-bot: FYI — no billing anomalies detected; RPM exhaustion doesn't imply billing error. If they want higher sustained rates, upgrade to Dedicated or request quota increase.

devin.k: Final notes to include in the reply to customer: explain difference between RPM, TPM, and concurrency; mention context length indirectly affects concurrency; suggest client-side levers (concurrency limiter, batching, backoff) and options (model variant, dedicated capacity). Include a small code sample for a simple concurrency limiter (node-ish pseudo):
```js
const maxConcurrent = 4;
const queue = [];
async function enqueue(req) {
  while (running >= maxConcurrent) await sleep(100);
  running++;
  try { await callApi(req); } finally { running--; }
}
```

amanda.s: Thanks everyone — I'll close the escalation and advise AcmeGames to: cap parallelism, add backoff, trim contexts, and open a support ticket if they want Dedicated capacity. Marking resolved unless anything else? :white_check_mark:
support-bot: Marked resolved in ticketing system (TICKET-2048).
